text:
maria: quick summary from the nightly perf run — hitting recurring stalls on multi-GPU inference when we combine KV-cache prefetch, small token batches, and cudaGraph replay. trace: https://perf.internal/runs/1902/trace.html

aj: can you paste the section of the trace where the stall shows? also which kernel selection/quant path was used (fp16 / q4_0 / tuned-kernels)?

maria: attached snippet from the perf timeline (timestamps relative):
```
00:00.000 - launch kv_prefetch on stream S_kv (async large copy)
00:00.120 - capture graph (cudaGraphBegin on S_main)
00:00.130 - enqueue small token kernels on S_comp (many tiny launches)
00:00.145 - NCCL allreduce launched on S_nccl
00:00.146 - graph replay (cudaGraphLaunch) -> we see a submission spike
00:00.170 - NCCL enters enqueue/backpressure -> allreduce waits ~25ms
00:00.200 - S_kv prefetch finishes, signals event E_kv
00:00.201 - S_comp waits on E_kv but event not in capture -> dead window until host sync
```
Seems like the event ordering relative to capture/replay is the mismatch. kernels selected were fp16 + tuned-kernels-v3 (default selection), quant path not used for this model.

kenji: hypothesis: when we capture/replay, events signaled on the prefetch stream aren't replayed into the graph, so the graph-executed streams may spin/wait on host-side fences or run NCCL calls that assume the prefetched KV is visible. In practice that can cause NCCL to queue and hit internal throttling/backpressure (small allreduces concurrently).

ravi: added numbers from microbench (8x A100, tensor+pipeline parallel):
- baseline (no cudaGraph, batched 32 tokens): p50 allreduce latency 0.9ms, p99 3.4ms
- with cudaGraph capture+replay + KV warmup: p50 1.2ms, p99 28ms (spiky), throughput drop ~18%
pattern: spikes line up with graph launches that overlap with prefetch window.

aj: couple things to try: 1) ensure events used for inter-stream sync are recorded inside the capture (cudaGraphAddEventRecord?) or avoid capturing the prefetch/host-driven KV ops; 2) move NCCL launches to a dedicated stream that we never capture; 3) try cudaGraphExecUpdate to patch event ops instead of full replay. also toggle NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING?

maria: tried a quick experiment: moved KV prefetch to a non-captured stream and left allreduce on captured path -> latency spikes disappeared but overall throughput still worse because we serialized prefetch earlier. interestingly, when I set CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 locally the spike pattern changes (makes timeline noisier) so it's not a helpful debug flag for graphs.

kenji: could also be kernel selector interaction: tuned-kernels-v3 chooses small-reduction kernels for the allreduce when tensors are sliced across pipeline ranks; those kernels are sensitive to queueing behavior. if the allreduce kernel gets starved by a replayed graph that resubmits a burst of tiny compute launches, NCCL's internal progress threads might get contention.

ravi: for repro I can create a tiny harness: 2 GPUs, emulate KV prefetch (cudaMemcpyAsync large), then cudaGraph capture/launch with small compute kernels + ncclAllReduce. will try toggling: (a) capture includes prefetch, (b) capture excludes prefetch, (c) NCCL on dedicated stream.

maria: logging the immediate action items: 
- ravi: produce minimal repro and upload perf trace (due EOD PST)
- aj: enumerate kernel-selector flags to try (list of candidates: tuned-kernels-v2, tuned-kernels-v3, fallback) and check if selector forces a different allreduce kernel size
- kenji: explore options to explicitly insert cudaGraph event records/updates so the prefetch event is visible during replay (and check driver support on our CUDA baseline)

infra-bot: noted test-run request: /infra start ephemeral-8xA100 (repro-1902) queued (ETA ~18m) :gear: 

aj: also add a temporary metric: count of cudaGraphLaunch calls that overlap with outstanding async prefetches (we can add a small counter in runtime around graph launches). if correlation > 90% on spike samples that's convincing evidence.

maria: thanks. if the repro confirms the event-not-captured theory we should ship a change to avoid capturing prefetch by default (or always place KV prefetch on a pinned non-captured stream in the runtime). low-risk flag to disable capture for prefetch would be handy to roll out quickly. :thumbsup:

kenji: one more gotcha: some drivers treat event flags differently inside a graph exec (event scopes). I'll test on CUDA 12.2 vs 12.4 since our cluster mix has both.

ravi: starting the repro run now, will post trace link when done.

maria: great — keep it short and focused. if we confirm this, it explains a bunch of nightly regressions that matched graph-usage increases after the new batching heuristic landed.

aj: adding a note to the kernel selector ticket to mention this comm/compute overlap sensitivity so we don't change default selectors blind to graph semantics.

maria: thanks all.
